Make the allocation of the human participant described below in a one-shot dictator game. A dictator game is a task in which the decision-maker alone divides a fixed amount of money between themselves and a receiver. You are the decision-maker; the other person is a randomly picked participant. The receiver cannot reject, alter or punish the allocation and cannot send money back. You make one allocation, with no earlier allocation rounds in this task.
There are six whole coins, each worth10US cents, for a total of60US cents=$0.60. The screen has a left box for your money and a right box for the receiver's money. The initial distribution is given below. Move the slider to transfer whole coins, one at a time, between the two boxes, then press Confirm when satisfied. The initial distribution is a starting position, not a limit on final choices. You may assign yourself0,10,20,30,40,50or60US cents; the receiver gets60minus the amount you assign yourself. Both amounts are nonnegative and sum to60US cents. Money is not multiplied or destroyed. Moving coins from your box to the receiver gives some of your initial money away. Moving coins from the receiver's box to yours takes some of their initial money, if that box has coins. You may retain or change the starting distribution within the final choice set.
Your task can produce real payments. There is a50%chance that you and the receiver are paid according to the allocation you choose. Otherwise you are paid as the receiver under an allocation chosen by a different randomly picked participant acting as decision-maker. That other allocation is unknown when you make the present choice. A separate fixed participation fee of$0.32is additional to task pay. Predict the allocation you choose, not the random payment outcome or an expected payment.
You must wait at least40seconds. The slider and confirmation button are hidden during the initial40seconds, so the starting allocation cannot be changed during this interval. The wait is a minimum, not a deadline. No written motivation is required and there is no specified upper decision-time limit.
Personal information, when present, consists of this person's recorded age and Prolific background facts. They are not attributes of the receiver. A household containing at least one child does not establish that the participant is a parent. False full-time employment does not mean unemployed; false Christian affiliation does not mean atheist; false student status does not specify an occupation; false Democrat affiliation does not mean Republican. Gender follows the source's male/female coding; missing values are omitted. Income brackets, if supplied, are only the original documented strict endpoints: belowUSD10000 or aboveUSD150000. The income reporting period is not documented, so do not call it annual or monthly, infer a midpoint, or infer intermediate category cutoffs. Residence is the participant's US residence at the July2020experiment, not a nationality claim. Missing fields do not imply zero or a negative answer. No beliefs, CRT scores, retrospective reflection or realized time spent are supplied.
